podcast.body: A love song from the *Wave* album, co-written with Richard Sohl, described as spiritual and gentle. Patti Smith refused to change the lyric "heroin," clarifying it referred to "feminine heroin" rather than a drug. The song was later used as the theme music for the Netflix series *Daisy Jones in the Six*, though it did not chart on Billboard. Robert Christgau hailed it as "quite possibly her greatest track ever." "That line where she says the word heroin She was told, oh you have to change that We don't want any drug references She says I'm not changing that, this is not a drug reference It's the feminine heroin."

podcast.body: This song was the best-known single from Patty Smith's 1979 album *Wave*. It became her most covered song, second only to "Because the Night," indicating its lasting appeal and influence. "Dancing barefoot, its best known single would become Smith's most covered song after because the night."
